keyframe_review.note: Shape unchanged (32,241 km2, 131 cells), status changed. Gazetteer check (mine): 114 of the 131 cells are the Provence region (121 cells), including all of Alpes-de-Haute-Provence and Vaucluse, so the row is Frankish Provence, not an empire; it lies wholly inside Cliopatria's Kingdom of the Franks shape of 705-717, i.e. a double cover. Provence 'was formally subject to the Frankish kings' (Provence page, 'during the late 7th and the early 8th centuries'). The Francia page does not describe the Merovingian realm as an empire (the Carolingian Empire dates from 800) and its infobox gives only '814 (peak): 1,200,000 km2' for all Francia, so no area comparison applies. Draw in the Frankish colour, not as a separate state; the lighter tint of rule 4 would fit 'formally subject'.

correction.text: the same Provence shape, still formally subject to the Frankish kings, in the Frankish colour

keyframe_review.note: Same 131-cell Provence shape as the 710 row, status changed as there. Here it is not a double cover: Cliopatria's Frankish shape for 718-723 (2,000 cells, 44.2 N southward limit) contains none of these cells, so this row alone keeps Provence on the map in those years and should not be dropped unless the Frankish dossier adds Provence back. Provence 'was formally subject to the Frankish kings' (Provence page, 'during the late 7th and the early 8th centuries'). No page dates a Carolingian takeover of Provence before 737-739 (Charles Martel in the Rhône valley, Avignon and Arles, 'chase the duke Maurontus to his stronghold of Marseille'), so the 718 relabelling is Cliopatria's, not a page's.

region.text: Frankish Provence, 'formally subject to the Frankish kings'

ledger.note: 710: Cliopatria begins a separate 'Merovingian Empire' row on Provence. The page dates no founding: Provence 'was formally subject to the Frankish kings' in the late 7th and early 8th centuries and 'the Franks in the 6th century' were its last conquerors. Bookkeeping start, confidence 1; the land is not new to the Franks.

718: Cliopatria relabels the same Provence patch 'Carolingian Empire'. The Francia page dates that empire to 800 ('In 800, it evolved into the Carolingian Empire'), and 718 is only the year of Charles Martel's victory at Soissons ('Charles defeated his rivals and forced them into hiding'). Same state, same colour (rule 2).

region.text: Provence, returning inside the Frankish shape

ledger.note: 723: Cliopatria ends the Provence row and its Frankish row takes Provence back in 724 (Frankish shape 724-731 contains all 131 cells). The Provence page's next dated events are Charles Martel's Rhône valley campaigns of 737 and 739 against the Umayyad garrisons of Avignon and Arles and the duke Maurontus, after the end of this row; the Francia page has 'Around 736 Duke Maurontus of Provence called in the Umayyads'.

certainty.note: Provence's frontier with the Umayyads of Septimania and with Burgundy and Italy is unfixed; no treaty or survey line.

notes: Cliopatria rows: 'Merovingian Empire' (710-717) and 'Carolingian Empire' (718-723) share one 131-cell, 32,241 km2 outline (Provence) and the Wikidata id Q146246 with 'Kingdom of the Franks' (462-849, owned by another part of group eu-07): all three are the one Frankish state, and the shared-Wikidata rule would put the dossier under the earliest slug, kingdom-of-the-franks, which is not mine. These two leaf rows are written here as one dossier (the earlier of the two slugs, both Names in cliopatria_names); the owner of kingdom-of-the-franks can absorb it. Colour: both rows should take the colour of kingdom-of-the-franks (family france, 'the Franks blue-violet'). Cliopatria's Frankish shape for 718-723 omits Provence (the hole this row fills) and its 705-717 shape includes it (a double cover). The umbrella entities (Merovingian Empire) and (Carolingian Empire) are not territory. Not settled in two pages: who really ruled Provence 710-723 (patricius, duke) and the extent of Frankish authority; open 'Duke Maurontus', 'Abbo' and 'Charles Martel' if wanted. No capital: the pages give none for Frankish Provence, so capitals is empty. No gazetteer names needed (Provence region exists).
